Stopped by to assist with a funding issue related to the merchant’s banking information. The account had several thousand dollars in pending funding due to a mismatch between the routing and account information on file. I spent approximately one hour working with Katie, the owner, and the owner’s wife to identify the source of the problem.

After reviewing the information, we determined that the owner had a debit/credit card replaced after it was stolen but continued using older checks that did not match the current account information. This created confusion and resulted in ACH processing issues. We worked through the details and expect to have a corrected ACH form submitted shortly with the proper banking information. Once the updated information is received and processed, funding should be directed to the correct account and the issue should be resolved.

Despite these challenges, Leon stated that he continues to promote EasyPay and plans to keep offering it as a financing solution. At this time, he reported no questions or concerns.

In the meantime, he’s been using KOALAFI quite a bit. Subject: 00UTO00000cRwzi2AC
Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Spoke with Sabrina, the manager. After several months of follow-up visits encouraging the shop to use EasyPay again, they are finally back on board and are now running EasyPay first. They are once again producing the same level of business they did with us when we were RIC, which is a great win.

This is a good example of how consistent relationship-building and periodic follow-up can help re-engage inactive merchants over time.

Sabrina shared that overall business has been slower, but higher repair costs have resulted in larger average ticket sizes, helping offset the decrease in car count. Based on their current activity, I estimate they have the potential to fund approximately $8K–$10K with EasyPay each month.

The shop is currently on a $20 spiff. Sabrina requested a poster, which I will provide once they are back in stock. I reminded her to reach out to Connor or me if she needs any assistance.

I spoke with Tre, the manager. He said he really likes the program and has made EasyPay his go-to financing vendor. He prefers EasyPay over KOALAFI because we do not require him to separate parts and labor on repair orders. He explained that he only uses KOALAFI when EasyPay does not approve enough to cover the full repair.

Tre mentioned that he has had some issues in the past regarding sales tax on invoices. Connor previously reviewed the proper procedures with him. He asked me how the tax exemption works and whether the shop could get in trouble for not charging sales tax. I showed him the Georgia reseller tax ID number located in his Business Center and advised him to have the owner provide that number to their tax professional, who would know how to handle it appropriately.

Tre had no other questions or concerns. I left behind a few EasyPay pens and notepads and reminded him to reach out to Connor or me if he ever needs assistance.

Full Comments:
Called and spoke with Robert. Our conversation focused primarily on the recent application declines he has been experiencing. He shared that **EasyPay is the only financing option** they offer, so when customers are declined, they often have no alternative way to finance their repairs.

Robert provided two recent examples that have been frustrating for both him and his customers. One customer had previously completed a lease with EasyPay but was declined when applying again. Another customer was initially approved, but after the approval expired and they reapplied, the second application was denied.

Robert expressed frustration with these situations because EasyPay is their only financing solution for customers who cannot pay the full repair cost upfront. I acknowledged his concerns, thanked him for the feedback, and encouraged him to continue reaching out whenever he encounters situations where we may be able to assist.

Full Comments:
Called and identified Jeff as the manager for the location. Brian is listed as the owner. I was able to gather additional shop potential information, including a **lower average repair order of approximately $450**.

Jeff shared that they currently work with **Snap Finance and Koalafi**. When discussing where EasyPay fits into their financing options, he explained that it depends on the customer, as they typically present multiple options and allow the customer to choose which provider they would like to move forward with.

I recommended that they consider running EasyPay first, as the program tends to perform best when it is presented before receiving declines from other financing providers. Jeff appreciated the feedback and thanked me for the suggestion.

I sent over my contact information and encouraged him to reach out if any questions or concerns come up.

EasyPay remains their go-to financing option. His only concern was the approval rate. We reviewed his dashboard and found that they had submitted eight applications, with two approvals. The positive takeaway is that they funded both approved applications, giving them an excellent pull-through rate.

I explained what I’ve been telling other shops: in the current economy, many customers are falling behind on payments, which negatively impacts their credit profiles and results in more financing declines. He understood and had no additional questions or concerns. I reminded him to reach out to Connor or me if he needs anything.

Subject: 00UTO00000dfder2AA
Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Connected with Jeff, the store manager. I noticed that they quickly funded an application with us when they first enrolled but haven’t run any applications since, so I reached out to check in and make sure everything was okay.

Jeff shared that business has slowed down significantly over the past couple of weeks. He believes this is largely due to kids going back to school and parents adjusting to a different routine. He’s hopeful that business will pick back up over the next couple of weeks.

I also noticed that Jeff had not redeemed his spiff, so I showed him how to do so. He said he didn’t feel comfortable redeeming it until he spoke with the owner to confirm that the owner didn’t want the funds to go toward the shop. In the meantime, I showed him how to register himself as a rewards user.

I left some swag and let him know to reach out if he needs any assistance.

He emphasized that they like EasyPay, want to use us, and want to send business my way, but the current issue is making the process difficult for their team.

Based on the consistency of what he described, this appears to be a potential technical/process issue worth investigating rather than an isolated customer issue. Need to escalate ...

Full Comments:
I spoke with Dan, the owner. They have had a wonderful July and August. He said these are his biggest months because people are purchasing phones, computers, and tablets for back-to-school.

Dan said he would be doing even more business with us if he received more approvals, but he understands that people’s credit has been challenging in the current economy. His only callout was that he wishes we had higher approval amounts and could go beyond our $5,000 limit. I explained that we occasionally approve up to $6,000, but that is rare and typically only occurs with customers who have extremely strong credit.

He did not have any other callouts or questions. I noticed he was running low on marketing materials, so I ordered more for the store. I also told him to reach out to Connor or me if he needed any assistance.

I also printed out a QR code and placed it in their waiting area so customers can easily apply on their own. Hopefully, this will help drive a little more busin...

We also reviewed the available early purchase options and discussed how they work so he can accurately explain them to customers and answer any related questions.
